findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to Internet-reachable attack paths and future security-group changes.
The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and snapshots unencrypted at rest. Unauthorized access to underlying storage or snapshots could expose database contents.
The EC2 instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its instance credentials would allow broad control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources.

The database password is interpolated into EC2 user_data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data can be retrieved by processes with instance access (including the instance metadata service) and is retained in Terraform state, increasing the risk of credential disclosure.
